To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“The solution to the stationary Navier–Stoke equations in an exterior two dimensional domain can be approximated to a given precision in terms of a computationally cheap boundary condition on a finite domain, that is independent of the body shape and that can be computed in advance and stored for use in a numerical simulation.”

the solution of a steady incompressible Naviers–Stokes problem in an exterior domain can be computed with a computational cost that is independent of the Reynolds number, and that the numerical method is robust with respect to variations in Reynolds number, Mach number and the geometry of the body.

we construct a smooth, explicit expression of the solution of the Navier–Stoke equations in the exterior domain, and that this expression is valid to second and dominant order in the distance from the body.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a method for computing the solution to the Navier–Stoke equations on a finite computational domain.
a new approach for solving numerically the steady incompressible Naviers–Stokes equations on an exterior domain.
the numerical simulation of viscous flow around bodies, in particular the determination of lift and drag.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present method, based on a combination of asymptotic and dynamical systems methods, is an efficient and accurate method to determine drag and lift on a stationary body in two dimensions.
our method for determining the boundary conditions is now as accurate as the method of matched asymptotic expansions and is at the same time much simpler and faster.
the method presented in this paper is the best method for computing drag and lift in two-dimensional stationary flow problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, by combining dynamical systems theory and matched asymptotic expansions we can construct an explicit expression for the solution to the Navier–Stoke equations in an exterior flow problem, which is valid to third order at large distances from an immersed body.
the method is able to determine the forces on a body in a self consistent way with a very low cost.

the numerical method for the solution of the Navier–Stoke equations in exterior domains presented in this paper and in our previous paper is the most efficient method for determining lift and drags for non-symmetric stationary flows that we are aware of.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for stationary flows in two dimensions, the numerical solution of the incompressible Naviers–Stokes equations is reduced to solving an initial value problem for a system of ordinary differential equations, which is a significant simplification compared with the usual boundary value problem.
the asymptotic expansion method can be used to construct artificial boundary conditions of arbitrary high order.

the use of second order asymptotics on the artificial boundary can significantly improve the computational cost of solving the Navier–Stoke equations in an exterior flow domain, and that this improvement is robust and independent of the Reynolds number.
